newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie asks judge to shun jail sentence.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie asks judge to shun jail sentence.

text.p: Bankrupt French tycoon Bernard Tapie asked a presiding judge "not to send me to jail" on Saturday at his trial for embezzling funds from Marseille soccer club.

On Wednesday a public prosecutor urged the court to jail the former soccer boss for two years, with another two years suspended, called for a two-million franc ($347,000) fine, and a suspension of civic rights for five years.

"I was a great star. For the past three years I have suffered everything, I have been ruined, dishonoured, humiliated. And you are asked to insist on the only thing left to me: the possibility of being in touch with my family," former cabinet minister Tapie told the court.

The court is due to rule on July 4 in a case which has failed to determine where the embezzled funds ended up and which has highlighted widespread illegal practices including false invoicing and kickbacks.
The public prosecutor had said that as far as Tapie was concerned "the end justifies the means, with no regard for the morality of sport".

Tapie, 54, is charged with embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) when he was president of the Marseille club. He is standing trial in the Mediterranean port city while serving an earlier jail sentence for fixing a match.
The trial was repeatedly suspended earlier this month after he spent 19 hours in a coronary intensive care unit after suffering chest pains and breathing difficulties.

Tapie went to prison nearly four months ago after the supreme court upheld an eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game, days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the embezzlement case. He is charged with swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.
